paragraphs.source_en: In truth, Konomi's thoughts were much the same as Sukezaemon's. She too felt certain that Sukeza would face danger within the next two or three days. Of course, it was Ieyasu who had let her know, all the while pretending that nothing was amiss... No sooner had Ieyasu and the Kita no Mandokoro left the Taiko's sickbed than one supposed version of the Taiko's last wishes after another began to emerge.

paragraphs.source_en: Not only in the port of Sakai, but throughout Kyoto and Fushimi, people were saying that whatever Luzon Sukezaemon did, Naya Shōan was directing him from behind the scenes... Taking advantage of Ieyasu's musings aloud, Konomi sounded him out obliquely: “Konomi would like to visit her father.”

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu tacitly gave his consent. Before leaving Fushimi, Konomi had intended to make a special visit to Chaya Shirōjirō and set out only after learning the particulars. But time was pressing, so she changed her mind at the last moment and went directly to the port of Sakai. Looking back now, she was glad she had done so, though she also felt a faint regret.

paragraphs.source_en: Hideyoshi's illness showed no sign of recovery; the blossom viewing at Daigo had likely been his final farewell to this mortal world. And Konomi was often seized by the feeling that the gathering that day might also have been her own last chance to behold the beauty of Japan. As these thoughts ran through her mind, Konomi suddenly covered her face and wept. It was not from overwhelming grief; but how could she not be deeply heartsick when she was about to set off for an unknown world?
